tables.name: Table of contents

It lists 'General Funds Revenue Chart 25' and 'FY 2022 Receipts 26' but on the actual pages 25 is the FY2023 receipts table and 26 is the pie chart — reversed, and the receipts are FY2023, not FY2022. Several entries read 'No Report Submitted' with no page (Agricultural Commission, Architectural Preservation District Commission, Green Communities, Historical Commission, Housing Authority).

tables.name: Town meeting article record with vote tallies
tables.printed_heading: 2022 TOWN MEETING EXCERPTS [sic] / Annual Town Meeting - May 6, 2023 (p162); Excerpts: SPECIAL TOWN MEETING November 14, 2023 (p172)

tables.notes: The header printed above the May 6 2023 meeting says '2022 TOWN MEETING EXCERPTS' — the wrong year. This is the richest structured content in the report for budget purposes: it names the exact transfer sources and amounts for each vote (e.g. Article 4 amends the FY23 budget by naming each line number and amount moved; Article 5 moves $1,500,000 of Free Cash to the Overlay Account for FY23 abatements; Article 7 raises $41,362,299.88 plus six named transfers for a FY24 total of $42,584,048.95; Article 6 funds the FY24 Capital Plan at $1,039,010). Two-thirds thresholds are printed with the tally ('66 YES, 8 NO - 50 needed for 2/3rds majority'). Pages 174-185 are mostly the full text of zoning bylaw amendments (Water Supply Protection District, self-storage, solar parking canopy, driveway standards) with a vote at the end. TWO PROMISED TABLES ARE MISSING FROM THE TEXT: the revolving fund spending limits after Article 2 (p162 ends 'for the spending limits as follows:') and the FY24 Capital Plan project list after Article 6 (p163 ends 'as follows:') — the next page begins with the next article in both cases.

tables.layout: three pages of a two-column numbered list with dollar amounts right-aligned; function subtotals interleaved (Total Gen Gov Unclassified, Total General Government, Total Central Purchasing, Subtotal Police, Subtotal Fire Dept., Total Protection, Total Health & Sanitation, Total DPW, Total Facilities & Bldgs, Total Solid Waste/Recycling, Total Assistance, ...)
tables.printed_total: No grand total is printed on the table itself; the total is in the Article 7 vote text on p164: 'Fiscal Year 2024 of $42,584,048.95'
tables.notes: The extracted table BEGINS mid-list at line 13/Reserve Fund — lines 1 to 12 (debt service, insurance, retirement, workers comp and similar) did not come through OCR and are effectively missing from the text layer. Line numbers are the same ones the town meeting votes reference by number ('line #13A/Salary Reserve'), which makes this the key to reading the article votes. Several line names are OCR-mangled: 'Neatoba Board of' (Nashoba), 'Nasheba Nursing', 'Funnelek Exe-Stal', 'T2A'. Some amounts lost their decimal point ('161.94240' for Building Inspector, '49.00000' for Animal Control). Largest lines: School Department $22,883,442.00, Monty Tech Assessment $1,181,390.00, Police $2,306,293.24, Fire $1,550,992.68.

tables.name: Annual town election official tally
tables.printed_heading: ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION / Saturday, May 20, 2023 / OFFICIAL TALLY
tables.what_it_is: Votes cast for every candidate for every elected office, by precinct, with blanks and 'All Others' and the ballot total for each contest.
tables.grain: one candidate (or Blanks / All Others row) within one office
tables.layout: two pages, heading repeated; each office is a block with a title row giving the term and number of seats, candidate rows, then All Others / BLANKS / TOTAL
tables.printed_total: Each contest prints its own TOTAL row: 1276 for two-seat contests, 638 for single-seat contests
tables.notes: '**' after a name means ELECTED (the key is printed at the foot of both pages). One contest records 'Failure to Elect' as a row (Sewer Commissioner, two seats, only one candidate). A few precinct cells are blank where OCR dropped a digit — the row totals still print. Eleven offices across the two pages. Turnout is implied: 1276/2 = 638 ballots cast.

tables.name: Town and school employee gross wages
tables.printed_heading: (section banner 'MISCELLANEOUS INFORMATION' on p189; the ToC calls it 'Town & School Employee Gross Wages 190')
tables.what_it_is: Every town and school employee's gross wages for the year, name by name. This is the report's payroll disclosure.
tables.layout: eight pages of a multi-column alphabetical name list with an amount column; printed small and dense
tables.notes: SEVERELY degraded in the text layer — only about 14-35 fragments survive per page, mostly surnames (BIERY, CALL, CORTEZ, DONELL, WARD, WEISS, WILDER) with the odd first name and the odd amount (73.38, 31.12, 53.44). The wages themselves are almost entirely absent from the extraction. Anyone wanting this data must re-OCR the PDF pages with column geometry. Identified only via the table of contents — nothing on pages 190-197 says what the list is.

tables.name: Town office hours and phone directory
tables.what_it_is: Department-by-department office hours and phone numbers.
tables.layout: three-column directory on the inside back cover
tables.notes: Most department names dropped out of the text layer; the hours and phone numbers survive without their labels. Carries the caveat line '(Please check the Town Website for any changes/updates to office /tours or meetings.)'

surprises: The revenue table is not called revenue. It is headed 'FY 2023 RECEIPTS - JUNE 2023' with a 'SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS' recap and a 'GRAND TOTAL' — on page 25, printed sideways, and the table of contents mislabels it 'FY 2022 Receipts' and puts it on the wrong page. That combination is almost certainly why earlier searches concluded this year has no revenue table.
Pages 49-51 are pages 2, 3 and 4 of a nine-page trust fund schedule — the town printed three pages of a longer document into the annual report and the other six pages exist somewhere else entirely.

Pages 190-197 are eight pages of every town and school employee's gross wages, and nothing on those pages says so; only the table of contents identifies them. The text layer has lost almost all of it.

Two tables the warrant articles explicitly promise ('for the spending limits as follows:' after Article 2, and the FY24 Capital Plan 'as follows:' after Article 6) simply are not in the document — the page turns straight to the next article. The Capital Planning Committee report on p108 likewise describes a 12-item, $2,025,010 plan and then does not print it.
The fire department's own call breakdown does not add up: 356 + 1193 + 366 + 18 = 1,933 against the 2,033 stated in the sentence above it.
The 'Collection of Taxes' receivables schedule on pages 54-56 is headed JUNE 30, 2023 but carries a sub-heading reading 'FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES' on all three pages.

The Board of Assessors report (p45-46) contains no valuation or tax rate table at all — just a narrative about 440 abatement applications against 14 the prior year, a 100% turnover of the board, and a delayed five-year revaluation. The only tax rate in the whole report is the single line 'FY'23 TAX RATE- $14.62' on the profile page.

The report carries the regional dispatch district's full statistics for eight other communities (Berlin, Bolton, Boxborough, Devens, DoD, Harvard, Lancaster, Townsend), five years deep — data about other towns, inside Lunenburg's annual report.
Monty Tech reports its FY23 grants as $2,963,607 in the figure block and $3,552,996 in the prose on the same page.
